title: Sharkey Bonano replacing Bix in the Wolverines
summary: Hug explains why Sharkey's style did not suit the Wolverines and how it affected him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Was Sharky, did you also play with Sharky?
Oh, I played with Sharky many times. Yes, many, many, many times.
Of course, he went to, he took Bix's place in the Wolverines.
They sent him to take Bix's place when Bix left the Wolverines. That's right.
I'm not sure he stayed too long.

No, he didn't stay too long because the truth of the matter is, is that it was a very hard thing for Sharky to take, I'm sure, because it did not prove successful for Sharky to go there and take Bix's place. You know, that was a tough job to ask anybody to do, any trumpet player to go and take Bix's place at that particular time.
Well, how could he fit the style of that band?

And it wasn't his style. And you know, this, I think, really did something to Sharky because he never would say very much if you mentioned Bix around him. And I can understand it, you know, I mean, it kind of gave him a terrible complex, I guess. But really, he wasn't deserving of this because it was a mistake. I think it was Paul Merez or someone who thought that Sharky could fill that bill, you see. Oh, I see. But Sharky's style, as Dick Allen says, anyone who knew Sharky would just know that Sharky was not the top trumpet player to play the style that Bix was playing.
